newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-BOK COACH OPENS DOOR FOR PIENAAR, STRANSKY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-BOK COACH OPENS DOOR FOR PIENAAR, STRANSKY.

text.p: New Springbok coach Carel du Plessis has taken the first step towards rehabilitating Francois Pienaar and Joel Stransky in international rugby.

Speaking at a news conference to announce his assistants in the top job, du Plessis said, "I am aware that Francois and Joel are playing good rugby at the moment. I have asked SARFU's (South African Rugby Football Union) director of coaching Rudi Joubet to provide me with videos of them in action in England.
"It is important that we achieve consistency in selection and we will try to be fair and not confine ourselves to players who are competing in South Africa.''
Du Plessis's predecessor as Springbok coach, Andre Markgraaff, discarded Pienaar at the end of last season, prompting the World Cup winning captain to accept a playing post at English club Saracens.
Stransky moved to Leicester for similar reasons and both appeared to have no chance of playing for South Africa again until now.
SARFU has completed the reshaping of the Springbok administrative set- up with the appointment of a new manager and assistant coach to du Plessis who was chosen as coach two weeks ago.
Former Springbok flank forward Gert Smal will be du Plessis's coaching assistant, while Arthob Petersen steps in as manager.

Petersen, 45, is one of two black members of SARFU's executive committee, while Smal steps up from assisting the coaching of the South African A team on their recent tour to Britain. Petersen was the manager of that tour and also went to Britain and Ireland with the Springboks in 1994.
Du Plessis confirmed that the Springboks would play their first ever test against Tonga at Newlands in Cape Town on June 10 as a warm-up for the three-test series against the British Lions.
